text:
Avery Johnson: anyone have the latest demo deck link? also doing a 20-min exec demo tomorrow — which slides should I skip so we don’t get lost in weeds?

Markus Klein: yep. Latest canonical is on Confluence (v1): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/Pitch+Decks+-+Redwood+Demo+Deck+v1 (same content as the Drive copy).

Redwood Drive Bot: Shared file: “Redwood Demo Deck v1” https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RedwoodDemoDeckV1/view

Soojin Lee: for 20-min exec version, recommend:
- Keep: Title → “Why now”/problem → Redwood thesis (serving matters) → 2-3 proof points → quick live moment → ROI framing → next steps
- Skip: deep Console tour + detailed rollout mechanics unless they ask
- Keep security as 1 slide only (no appendix) unless there’s a security person on

Camila Reyes: +1. I’ve been using this run:
1) 1 slide: what we do (unified inference across hosted/dedicated/private)
2) 2 slides: production economics (cost/latency levers)
3) 1 slide: reliability (fallback/graceful degradation)
4) 1 slide: “how customers adopt” + next steps
If you do a live demo, do ONLY the chat streaming + structured output moment (2-3 mins).

Avery Johnson: perfect. when you say “skip deep Console tour” — which slide numbers in v1?

Soojin Lee: in v1, I’d skip ~slides 12–16 (Console deep dive + rollout views) for exec. You can keep the single dashboard screenshot slide if you want (it’s the one that shows token cost breakdown) but don’t click around live.

Markus Klein: if they want *some* product UI: do one static screenshot (latency/cost breakdown) + say “happy to go deep with your platform team.” Live clicking is where we’ve seen time sink + risk.

Elliot Price: talk track has an “Exec 20” variant callouts in the speaker notes now. Same link family: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/Demo+Talk+Track+Script+v1

Avery Johnson: amazing. any wording for Dedicated vs Hosted so I don’t confuse them in 20 min?

Camila Reyes: my quick line: “Hosted is fastest to start. Dedicated is the same API with reserved capacity + isolation + predictable throughput. Private is the same control plane patterns in your VPC/on-prem.” Then move on.

Markus Klein: + if you want, I can join for 5 mins at the end to handle reliability/security Qs. just ping.

Avery Johnson: thanks all — grabbing v1 deck + will trim. :thumbsup:
